title: Validate Signup
prompt: A TypeScript signup form needs simple client-side validation. Write a function that returns an array of error messages: require an email containing "@" and a password at least 8 characters long.

explanation.beginner:
Example: validateSignup({"email":"ada@example.com","password":"longpass"}) produces []. Check each independent constraint and associate failures with the field or rule that caused them.

Compare “reports both errors”: input [{"email":"bad-email","password":"short"}] produces ["Email must contain @","Password must be at least 8 characters"]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Check each independent constraint and associate failures with the field or rule that caused them.

Tempting mistake: Returning at the first error may hide other errors when the contract asks for all of them. Whitespace and empty strings need explicit treatment.

The reference uses includes. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “reports both errors”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
